name: Persistent Systems Ltd
about: Persistent Systems provides software engineering and strategy services to help companies implement and modernize their businesses. It has its own software and frameworks with pre-built integration and acceleration [1] . It also has partnership with providers such as Salesforce and AWS [2] .

statements.text: Revenue compounded 28.6% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 32.8%.
EBITDA margin expanded 270 bps over 5 years (16.3% → 19.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 23% to 30% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 13.6%, 550 bps below a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹5,969 cr of profit, ₹6,027 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.01x.

ledger.quote: we want to be in the 16 to 17 % range, that is our aspiration
ledger.statement: Aspirational EBIT margin of 16-17% (management says this is not formal guidance)
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: No horizon, and management calls it an aspiration. Q2 FY27 EBIT margin was 15.0%, down 100 bps QoQ (so Q1 was about 16.0%) and 130 bps YoY (so Q2 FY26 was about 16.3%), driven by a 140 bps net wage-hike hit and lower utilisation (C2, C3). The company was at the bottom of the band and has now dropped below it.
ledger.actual_text: 15.0% EBIT margin in Q2 FY27 (C1, C2)

ledger.quote: We are confident of getting these approvals in over the next several weeks
ledger.statement: RBI and related approvals for the Nagarro combination expected within several weeks
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: Said on the Q2 FY27 call, a few weeks before the as-of date (15 Nov 2026). No later update is available.

ledger.quote: we will be raising USD 1.25 billion in terms of both debt and equity
ledger.statement: Raise USD 1.25 billion of debt and equity for the Nagarro acquisition financing (USD 450 million equity-linked)
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: Financing for the Nagarro deal, which has not closed (G6). No raise is reported in the inputs. Current borrowings are INR 575 crore at 0.07x D/E (F:borrowings_cr, F:debt_to_equity), so this raise changes the balance sheet materially; USD 450 million of it is equity-linked.

ledger.quote: we are expecting one-time expenses to the tune of approximately $50 million spread over three to four quarters
ledger.statement: One-time Nagarro transaction expenses of about USD 50 million over 3-4 quarters
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 booked INR 1,853.4 million of Nagarro transaction costs (C3), about USD 19.4 million at the quarter's implied INR 95.65/USD. Adding the guided USD 25-30 million still to come (G5) gives USD 44-49 million, in line with the about USD 50 million total.
ledger.actual_text: About USD 19.4 million booked in Q2 FY27 (C3)

ledger.quote: we expect an incremental amount ranging between USD 25 to 30 million
ledger.statement: Further USD 25-30 million of Nagarro transaction costs over the next two quarters (Q&A later says 3-4 quarters)
ledger.speaker: Tailwinds
ledger.evidence: Covers Q3-Q4 FY27, which have not been reported. The timing is internally inconsistent: two quarters in prepared remarks (C3) against three to four quarters in Q&A (G4).

ledger.quote: We expect in the next 4 to 6 weeks, max, let's say 8 weeks
ledger.statement: Close Nagarro deal (after Austria and Spain FDI approvals) within 4-8 weeks
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: The 4-8 week window from the Q2 FY27 call runs to about late December 2026. No later signal.

ledger.quote: we will need about 5 to 6 months to optimistically bring the 2 companies together
ledger.statement: Merger squeeze-out and integration of the two companies in about 5-6 months after closing
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: The 5-6 month clock starts at closing, which has not happened (G6).

ledger.quote: we expect this transaction to close sometime towards the Q4 of Calendar Year 2026 or early Q1 of Calendar Year 2027.
ledger.statement: Nagarro transaction expected to close around Q4 CY2026 to early Q1 CY2027
ledger.speaker: Vinit Teredesai
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 guided closing for Q4 CY2026 to early Q1 CY2027. The Q2 FY27 call narrows that to 4-8 weeks after the Q2 call (G6), i.e. within the window, subject to RBI and Austria/Spain FDI approvals (G2).

ledger.quote: So, at 50% plus 1 share to 100%, it is expected to reduce down to 1X by FY2030.
ledger.statement: Net debt to combined EBITDA to fall to about 1x by FY30
ledger.speaker: Vinit Teredesai
ledger.evidence: FY30 deleveraging target. The deal has not closed and no combined EBITDA or net debt is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: The transaction is expected to be Cash EPS accretive as well as Reported EPS accretive in Year 1
ledger.statement: Transaction expected to be cash and reported EPS accretive in Year 1
ledger.speaker: Vinit Teredesai
ledger.evidence: Year-1 accretion cannot be judged before closing. The Q2 FY27 transaction costs (INR 1,853.4 million) already cut reported PAT margin to 7.5% from an operating 10.6% (C1).

ledger.quote: to scale to the aspiration of $5 billion that we have? By FY31, we get that as well at a nice scale.
ledger.statement: Aspiration of USD 5 billion revenue scale by FY31
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: FY31 aspiration. The Q2 FY27 annualised run rate is about USD 1.95 billion (4 x USD 487.6 million), so reaching USD 5 billion needs about 2.6x growth in four and a half years, and much of that will presumably come from Nagarro.

ledger.quote: the $2 billion by FY27, that's a run rate
ledger.statement: Revenue run rate of USD 2 billion by FY27, within a quarter at worst
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: Clarified as a run rate. Q2 FY27 is USD 487.6 million, an annualised USD 1.95 billion, and Q2 grew 7.8% QoQ; reaching a USD 500 million quarter needs about 2.5% more over Q3-Q4. If Nagarro consolidates in Q4, the target will be met trivially and stop being an organic test.
ledger.actual_text: USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27 (about USD 1.95 billion annualised)

ledger.quote: Q4 exit is where we are looking at the run rate being in the range of $500 million or so
ledger.statement: Q4FY27 exit run rate of about USD 500 million
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27 (C1) leaves a 2.5% gap to the USD 500 million exit over two quarters, against 7.8% QoQ growth in Q2 alone. The same caveat applies: Nagarro consolidation would blur the organic read.

ledger.quote: Our aspiration continues to be in the 16 to 17% range.
ledger.statement: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17% (management says this is an aspiration, not guidance)
ledger.speaker: Vinit Teredesai
ledger.evidence: Aspiration set in Q4 FY26. Two quarters later, EBIT margin has gone from about 16.0% in Q1 FY27 to 15.0% in Q2 FY27, 130 bps lower YoY (C1, C2). The computed margin series also fell, from 18.9% to 16.2% to 13.6% (F:margin_last4_pct), though that series appears to include the Nagarro one-offs.

ledger.quote: advancing confidently towards our aspiration of $2 billion by March 2027
ledger.statement: Revenue aspiration of USD 2 billion by March 2027
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: On a run-rate basis, as clarified in G12, it is on track: the Q2 annualised rate is USD 1.95 billion. Read literally as FY27 revenue, it would be at risk: H1 is about USD 940 million (Q1 about USD 452 million plus Q2 USD 487.6 million), which needs H2 to average about USD 530 million a quarter.

ledger.quote: laying the foundation of $5 billion by March 2031
ledger.statement: Revenue foundation of USD 5 billion by March 2031
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: March 2031 horizon. It restates the G11 aspiration, and no progress measure beyond the current run rate is available.

ledger.quote: ETR for FY26 will be in the range of 20%-24%
ledger.statement: Effective tax rate for FY26 of 20-24%
ledger.speaker: Vinit Teredesai
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but the inputs give no FY26 effective tax rate. The only datapoints are Q1 and Q2 FY27 at 22.5% (C3), which fall inside the 20-24% range but are not the FY26 figure.

ledger.quote: we are not aspiring now to take it another 200
ledger.statement: No plan to pursue a further 200 bps margin expansion
ledger.speaker: Sandeep Kalra
ledger.evidence: A statement of what management will not pursue, with no testable target. It is consistent with the 16-17% cap in G1 and G14, and margins have since fallen rather than risen.

ledger.quote: There will be a further reduction in cost that will happen in FY27.
ledger.statement: Further cost reduction to occur in FY27
ledger.evidence: FY27 is not over, but Q2 shows cost action: lower ESOP costs absorbed 40 bps of the 180 bps wage-hike hit, and lower ESOP/SG&A plus currency added 150 bps of EBIT benefit (C2, C3). Despite that, overall EBIT margin still fell 100 bps QoQ.
ledger.actual_text: Lower ESOP and SG&A costs in Q2 FY27 (C2, C3)

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management says it does not give forward-looking guidance and frames the 16-17% margin as an aspiration, while deal timing depends on approvals that will come when they come (p19-41-1, p20-49-1).

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management is assertive on deal accretion, deleveraging and growth, while calling integration a slow, planned process.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says "we are confident, we are marching towards it steadily" about the revenue run-rate target.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says it remains firmly on track towards USD 2 billion by March 2027 and expects a further cost reduction in FY27, while noting that the margin gain is not expected to repeat.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Revenue growth is 'healthy': 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD, the 26th straight quarter of sequential growth (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: INR revenue grew 30.2% YoY and has accelerated for four quarters (23.4%, 25.1%, 29.1%, 30.2%). About 950 bps of the INR growth is currency, since constant-currency growth was 20.8%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The margin aspiration remains 16-17% EBIT, and the Q2 dip is the annual wage hike plus deliberate hiring ahead of large-deal ramps (G1, G14, C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: EBIT was 15.0%, down 130 bps YoY, so the drop is not just seasonal. The computed operating margin fell from 19.1% a year ago to 13.6%, and from 19.4% to 13.6% over four quarters (that series likely includes Nagarro deal costs). Utilisation slipped 70 bps to 85.8%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Underlying profit is intact; the reported PAT drop is a one-time Nagarro cost of about 3.1% of revenue (C1, C3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The one-off arithmetic holds: INR 1,853.4 million pre-tax at a 22.5% tax rate is about 3.1% of revenue, taking 10.6% to 7.5%. But operating PAT grew only 5% YoY on 30.3% INR revenue growth. Net other income swung to INR -131.2 million from +414.9 million, and reported PAT fell 25.3% YoY.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: In Q4 FY26, the OCF/PAT dip to 77% was blamed on unbilled revenue that would 'normalize in the next quarter' (C5).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The cash conversion cycle is 83 days, up from 69 three years ago, and Q2 FY27 finance costs rose because of 'higher receivables financing' (C3). That points to working capital being funded rather than normalised. Longer-run cash conversion is still sound, with five-year CFO/PAT 1.01 and FCF INR 4,405 crore.

bull.point: Revenue delivery is consistent: USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27, 26 straight quarters of sequential growth, and INR revenue growth accelerating to 30.2%. The USD 500 million Q4 exit target needs only about 2.5% more over two quarters.
Demand visibility: Q2 TCV of USD 633.5 million with ACV of USD 481 million, roughly one quarter's revenue. Headcount grew by 958 to staff large-deal ramps while attrition eased from 12.3% to 11.9%.

The pre-deal balance sheet can absorb the Nagarro financing: D/E 0.07 on borrowings of INR 575 crore, five-year FCF of INR 4,405 crore, CFO/PAT 1.01 and ROCE 34%, with leverage guided back to 1x net debt/EBITDA by FY30.

bear.point: Margins are moving away from target: EBIT margin is 15.0%, down 130 bps YoY and 100 bps QoQ, against a repeated 16-17% aspiration. The computed margin is 13.6% against 19.1% a year ago, and operating PAT grew just 5% on 30.3% INR revenue growth.

Nagarro brings dilution, debt and cost before any synergy: a USD 1.25 billion raise including USD 450 million equity-linked, about USD 50 million of one-off costs (USD 19.4 million already booked, taking reported PAT down 25.3% YoY), leverage at 1x only by FY30, and 5-6 months of integration after closing.

Working capital and treasury are getting worse: the cash cycle is 83 days against 69, receivables financing is rising, net other income is INR -131.2 million against +414.9 million last quarter, and Q2 had an FX loss of INR 455.8 million.

questions: Once Nagarro consolidates, how will you report organic revenue? On an organic basis, do you still expect a USD 500 million Q4 FY27 exit (G13) and a USD 2 billion run rate (G12)?
What is the bridge from 15.0% EBIT back to 16-17%: utilisation recovery from 85.8%, margins on the ramping large deals, or pricing? Where does the combined margin land after Nagarro?

Q4 FY26 said unbilled revenue would normalise in a quarter, yet Q2 FY27 shows higher receivables financing. What are billed and unbilled DSO today, and how much of the receivables book is factored or financed?
